correctness.rationale: For all n>=6, four forced blue sets form five symmetry orbits; first force gives exhaustive local classification. Each pair of four-sets is token-adjacent precisely at intersection size three. Checking the five orbit representatives under all dihedral shifts/layer swaps yields a quotient adjacency matrix with constant rows [0,0,4,4,4],[0,2,0,4,2],[2,0,0,4,2],[1,2,2,1,2],[1,1,1,2,0]. With orbit sizes n,2n,2n,4n,4n, row sums give n degree-12, 8n degree-8, 4n degree-5 and 48n edges. Squares Q_i connect to Q_(i+1) through one T-type state and each other type reaches a square in <=2 moves, so entire graph connected. Standalone independent brute-force checks n=6..15 and symmetry-generated checks n=24,40,80, but infinite claim follows from local templates.

value.rationale: The cyclic-prism family supplies an exact, nontrivial solution-space connectivity theorem beyond the known scalar optimum and static enumeration. Minimum sets can be navigated by single-token changes without leaving optimality. The 5x5 adjacency quotient and full degree profile, 48n edges and 4n odd-degree states describe local geometry and complexity of that feasible reconfiguration network; none is determined by the static 13n count alone.
